ratings.reason: Locating a privately held leaf depends on ownership correspondence that is mostly offline. The 1906 photo helps with identification but not with location. Finding it would recover one leaf of a key witness to Archimedes.
There is no document of optical aid use, and optical effects have competing explanations from image evidence alone. New public material is unlikely to settle the question.
The dispute turns on calendar conventions and event identifications that existing evidence cannot adjudicate without new finds. A secure date would anchor early Chinese chronology.
Recordings can be matched with discographies, family papers and the press, and the Grant lead is concrete. Each identification is small, but a method would extend to many cylinders.
The itinerary is internally inconsistent, and archaeology lacks a naming inscription. A century of debate suggests document analysis cannot decide between Kyushu and Kinai.
The 1808/1818 citation conflict can probably be resolved from the Latin source. Identifying the actual volcano still needs physical tephra evidence the team cannot obtain.
Rare graphs and name-only signs resist decipherment. Computational analysis may read some, but a convincing reading of 'thousands' as posed is unlikely.
Very short inscriptions limit statistical tests, and earlier entropy studies stayed inconclusive. A decisive answer would reshape South Asian prehistory.
Contract signatures support estimates of signing ability for a selective population. Extending that to population-wide reading remains an inference problem.
Post-contact sources and patchy archaeology leave estimates spanning an order of magnitude. Archival work alone will not close the range.
Provenance studies already point regionally, toward the Eritrea and Somali coasts. Transshipment through intermediate ports blocks precise location without new isotopic sampling.

The journals are online and the Cas A position is known, so the question is checkable. It depends on positional precision, and a negative answer may also be convincing. A result would refine the supernova's date.
Statistical tests on errors, precession and latitude-dependent visibility are tractable and have advanced already. A checkable verdict on the mixed origin is plausible.
Large-scale text mining with deduplication of quotations is well suited to an agent team. It can bound prevalence and its social distribution.
The extinction date depends on how unverifiable sightings are weighted. Archival work can sharpen the record but not resolve the probabilistic disagreement.
Dating requires lab and paleographic access, and coverage of variants is uneven. The question is contested and high-stakes, and synthesis alone is unlikely to settle it.
The evidence is indirect, regionally fragmented and already intensely debated (maximalist vs minimalist). A convincing mortality figure is unlikely.
Port reports and newspapers allow linking some shipments to first outbreaks. Farm-level delivery links remain the weak point.
A convincing answer needs aDNA or burial evidence, which is beyond the team's reach. Texts are sparse, and abandonment of settlements has many possible causes.
Registered flows can be compiled, but smuggling and Japanese silver keep totals model-dependent. A better-bounded estimate is feasible, a convincing one less so.
Rigorous chance-baseline tests are feasible and could convincingly reject families. A positive identification is very unlikely, so the chance credits mostly negative results.

The code is dictionary-based, and the published key pairs plus edition comparison should permit decryption of accessible letters. Some originals are hard to reach. Decryption would document Wilkinson's treason.
Age-specific mortality data exist and can be standardized. A checkable answer is likely, and it bears on epidemiological debates about the 1889 pathogen.
Dated drawings plus computed central meridians can test continuity. Ambiguity in the marks may leave a qualified answer. A result matters for the Spot's longevity.
Searchable Ming records help, but Aceh coverage is thin and a negative result is hard to make convincing. A find would aid hazard history.
Plausible routes via Surat are known, but tracing a specific bird needs a document that may not exist. The interest is mostly local.
Without excavation or a naming inscription, textual and satellite reasoning can only narrow candidate locations.
Comparability problems (in-kind pay, baskets, occupations) remain unresolved despite extensive prior work. New archival compilation may help modestly.
Dendro and radiocarbon work has narrowed the field toward the Middle Chronology. Integrating anchors could yield a defensible answer, but disputes persist.
Text-matching unattributed passages against digitized alchemical literature is tractable for an agent team. Repeated formulae complicate attribution, but many passages should resolve.
Linking present forest abundance to colonial planting needs field and genetic data. The archive alone gives correlation at best.
Makassan versus First Fleet origins remain contested. The chronological gap probably lacks documents, and the theory carries major political weight.
Decades of searching have produced no transmission document. New digitized Byzantine manuscripts give a small chance of a link.
Pathogen identification needs aDNA beyond existing published samples. Symptom texts are compatible with several diseases.
The corpus is small and carving dates are uncertain. Testing for post-1770 contact influence is possible, but a convincing verdict is unlikely.
The objects are lost and the transcriptions conflict. Linguistic analysis has recently revived the authenticity case, yet without the leather the question stays contested.
The lack of bilinguals is the binding constraint. Computational comparison may extend some lexicon, but full translation is unlikely.
Matching Hunayn's list against digitized manuscripts and quotations is a strong agent task. Partial identifications of lost works are plausible.
Fiscal quotas mask real counts, and wartime survival of records is uneven. The estimate range will stay wide.
Linguistic and metrical arguments are already exhaustively debated, and no new evidence class is available.
The high/low count dispute rests on interpreting the census jump, and survey evidence is heterogeneous. A decisive answer is unlikely.
A systematic chronicle database with dedup could map spread direction. Ambiguous notices limit certainty.
Cross-linking catalogues, labels and correspondence can name some enslaved and Indigenous informants. Many will stay unnamed, but partial answers are checkable.
Records are partial across empires and local carriers left little trace. A convincing total is unlikely, though a database would be valuable.
Image analysis can test the hand-mould hypothesis against the Agüera y Arcas/Paul Needham claims, but imaging artifacts confound it. Physical examination would be needed.
Borrowed passages can be detected by text reuse, giving strong negative evidence for some legs. Confirming the rest is harder.
The dispatch plus other VOC records may constrain timing. Rupture identification depends on coral and modeling ambiguity.
A smoking-gun letter is unlikely, and much correspondence is undigitized. Absence of evidence will not be convincing.
Matching footage to synopses and the trade press is well suited to agents, and identifications are checkable. Each is small, but they compound.
Euphemism and regional gaps prevent a convincing hemispheric total. Regional estimates are more feasible.
Accession records can trace some lineages. Genetics, which is beyond reach, would be needed for others. The work has conservation value.
The parallel Florentine texts and dictionaries are accessible, and a textual analysis answer is very feasible.
Systematic scanning of digitized books finds checkable lists, and the existing catalogue gives a baseline. This opens evidence for many languages.
Changes in register type and units confound the trend. Careful reanalysis may clarify but is unlikely to be decisive.
Few secure khipu–document pairings exist. Pattern analysis may show non-numeric structure, but reading signs is unlikely.
Textual comparison of the recipe and manuscript plus Sloane provenance trails is tractable. The route is the uncertain part. The result would credit an enslaved healer.
Dated contemporary documents can be sorted from retrospective accounts. A checkable earliest description is plausible.
The records concern officials, not growers. Other VOC records might add detail, but the answer is likely to stay thin.
Capture–recapture style estimation is feasible, but format biases make estimates model-dependent. A defensible range is possible.
Late notation of Old Roman melodies leaves the stemma underdetermined, and the debate is long-standing.
Collection-rate disputes underlie the competing estimates (Hartwell vs critics). Limited archaeology keeps it unresolved.
Deduplicating the depositions is a strong agent task for Protestant deaths. Coverage bias limits a full total.
The Sulu–Borneo leg is undocumented, and genetics, which is beyond reach, bears most of the evidential weight.
Image and text matching across IDP is tractable, and joins are checkable. It enables many manuscript studies.
Searchable transcriptions allow systematic join and duplicate detection, which specialists can verify. It feeds edition work.
The 'too good' statistics are established, but the 'why' lacks working records. The cause will stay speculative.
Comparing the Bern partbook with intabulations can test recovery of missing voices. Arranger changes limit fidelity, but many matches are checkable.
The intermediate links are lost, and the route via Mongols or the Islamic world stays inferential.
Many causal hypotheses fit uneven data, and records cannot isolate quarantine effects convincingly.
Text reuse across digitized newspapers can locate bylines. Propagated errors need care. It could recover many writers.
Structural analysis suggests some linguistic features, but proving language encoding and descent from short accounting texts is hard.
Damaged type and ornament matching has been proven at scale. Subscription access limits coverage, but checkable attributions are likely and broadly reusable.

prior_exposure: None known. I have general background on many of these debates from training, but no exposure to any ranking of this question set.
